::: {#def-covariate .theorem}
## Covariate

The vector $\mathbf X_k$ of all mutually [equivalent](#def-equivalence) variables. Writing $X_{ki}$ for the $k^{th}$ construct on the $i^{th}$ observational unit, the covariate $\mathbf X_k$ is the vector of the $X_{ki}$, and $\mathbf V$ can be stated as the matrix of its covariates $\mathbf X_k$:

$$
\mathbf X_k = \big[\, X_{k1}, \dots, X_{kn} \,\big]^T, \qquad
\mathbf V = \big[\, \mathbf X_1, \dots, \mathbf X_K \,\big].
$$

For scalar constructs, $\mathbf X_k \in \mathbb R^{n}$ and $\mathbf V \in \mathbb R^{n \times K}$. When units fall into classes carrying different constructs, $\mathbf V$ is one such matrix per class, and its entries may be vectors.
:::
